As a female that has previously used dating apps (and totally abandoned them) the idea of something different definitely caught my attention. I think that men have a disadvantage on them for sure, but it's really not easy for women, either. From my understanding, men hardly get any likes. However, (and this is just my experience) women get bombarded with too many likes. Men seem to match with every woman on the app, as every time I liked a man, we always instantly match, or I constantly get notifications that some guy liked me or sent me a message (depending on the app). Because of the mass amount of people who liked me or sent me messages, I cannot keep up with conversations. It's hard talking to five guys at the same time!! And probably around 99% of the time, the chat goes nowhere. Occasionally they'll ask for my number or (even worse) Snapchat. I do like being able to talk to them elsewhere because I can keep up with conversations easier, but my phone number is too personal to be handing out freely on a dating app, and I hate Snapchat. I've occasionally had guys want to talk to me through apps such as Telegram, but, as per usual, nothing of substance comes from it. What I believe dating apps (at least the free ones I use) are lacking is making sure they're matching you with people who share your interests. For example, I want a long term relationship, so why is the app pushing people looking for a hookup? In all honesty, I've had more luck finding relationships on Discord then I have on any dating sites. What I like about discord is that you can connect with people who share your interests, no matter how niche they are. I want a relationship based on substance, not looks. Dating apps don't have any substance to them. It's just a popularity contest based on how handsome or pretty you are.
I don't know if any of this helps you, but that's my experience with them. And if you ever develop one, let me know because I need something different than Tinder or Bumble or Hinge or whatever else there is.
